svg.title: Shirt back print — cppreference.com Friend declaration (transparent, multi-color)
svg.desc: Print-ready back styled as the cppreference.com Friend declaration page. White ink on transparent for dark shirts. Uses cppreference's actual font stacks (Linux Libertine for headings, Liberation Sans / DejaVu Sans for body, monospace for code).

text.font-family: 'Libertinus Serif', 'Linux Libertine', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif

g.text: The friend declaration appears in a class body and grants a function or another class access to private
and protected members of the class where the friend declaration appears.

g.font-family: 'Liberation Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: - the keyword typename followed by a qualified identifier

svg.text: 1) Designates a function or several functions as friends of this class:

g.font-family: 'Liberation Mono', ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

text.tspan: // the non-member function operator<< will have access

g.text: friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& out, const Y& o);
friend char* X::foo(int); // members of other classes can be friends too
friend X::X(char), X::~X(); // ctors and dtors can be friends
Friendship is not transitive (a friend of your friend is not your friend).
Friendship is not inherited (your friend’s children are not your friends, and your friends are
Access specifiers have no effect on the meaning of friend declarations (they can appear in
private: or in public: sections, with no difference).
A friend class declaration cannot define a new class (friend class X {}; is an error).
